tradition: The undivided church of the household congregations
presentBody: the Catholic Church, the Coptic Orthodox Church, the Church of the East and the Armenian Church, among others
basis: An early period of the church that is alive today. The churches that trace their bishops back to these congregations carry it, through the Roman church and the other ancient sees.
openQuestion: Is a period before the churches divided an episode of one living tradition, or only a root they all claim?

basis: A circle of writers whose works are still read. The entry describes books and arguments, and names no community that continued as its own body.
wanted: A dated source showing a community that continues the apologists as a body.

tradition: Latin apologetic writing, Tertullian to Lactantius
basis: A line of writers whose Latin terms and arguments are still used. The entry describes books and authors, and names no community that continued as its own body.
wanted: A dated source showing a community that continues the Latin apologists as a body.

tradition: Apocryphal and pseudepigraphal texts in Christian copying
basis: A body of texts that Christian scribes copied for centuries. The entry describes books, and names no community whose own life continued.
wanted: A dated source showing a community that uses these texts as its own tradition.

tradition: The Alexandrian catechetical school and its Christian-Platonist method
basis: A school and a way of reading Scripture. The method shaped later readers, but the entry names no community that kept the school going as its own body.
wanted: A dated source showing an unbroken school or community, not a later refounding or a claim of heritage.
openQuestion: Does the later catechetical teaching of the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria count as descent, or only as a claim of heritage?

tradition: Latin pastoral-congregational Christianity of Carthage and Hippo
basis: The congregations of Cyprian and Augustine were North African. The entry says that Latin Christianity's ideas about a local church "took shape largely in these two African towns". Their ideas passed to the Latin West, but the tree names no body that carries the African congregations.
endQuote: Latin Christianity's basic ideas about what a local church is took shape largely in these two African towns.
wanted: A dated source on the Catholic Church in North Africa that claims unbroken succession from the African congregations.
openQuestion: Is this the North African community (ended) or a period of the Latin church that the Catholic Church carries today?

basis: Its carriers ended. The entry's own text says the churches faded and that nothing descends from them. Its arguments shaped the church that answered it.
endQuote: Marcionite churches faded in the West by roughly the fourth century and lingered considerably longer in Syria and the East, but nothing descends from them.

tradition: Valentinian and other Gnostic Christian communities
basis: Its carriers ended. The entry's own text says no community survives and none claims descent. Modern groups that use the name are a later revival, not a continuation.
endQuote: No community survives, and none claims descent.

basis: Its carriers ended. The entry's own text says it had largely vanished by the sixth century and calls it an extinct religion. Its texts are read today, but no community continued.

basis: Its carriers ended. The entry's own text says the last Novatianist communities faded in the East by about the seventh century.
endQuote: No church descends from them; the last Novatianist communities faded in the East by around the seventh century.

basis: The entry follows two writers and their works, which are still read. It names no body that carried this circle forward as its own community.
wanted: A dated source linking a present church to the third-century church of Neocaesarea or Olympus.
openQuestion: Is this the Greek church of Anatolia in one period, which the Orthodox churches carry, or a circle of writers?

tradition: Origen's library and the scholars of Caesarea in Roman Palestine
basis: The entry follows a library and its scholars, Pamphilus and Eusebius. The books and the timeline they built are still used. The entry names no body that continued the Caesarea circle.
wanted: A dated source linking a present church to the Caesarea school.
openQuestion: Is this the local church of Palestine, which the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem carries, or a circle of scholars?

tradition: The Roman church in the third century
basis: An episode of a living tradition. The Roman church of Callistus and Hippolytus is the earlier life of the Catholic Church, which is alive today.

tradition: Latin biblical commentary in the Danubian provinces
basis: The entry follows one commentator, Victorinus of Pettau, whose reading of Revelation passed into the West. It names no body that continued the Danubian churches as its own community.
wanted: A dated source linking a present church to the Danubian congregations.

basis: The tradition reaches today through the Coptic monastic revival. The entry itself says monks inhabit the monasteries of St Antony, St Paul and Wadi al-Natrun today.

tradition: The Cappadocian fathers and their pastoral and monastic work
basis: The Cappadocian fathers are venerated in several churches today, and the entry says so. Veneration and shared texts are influence. The entry names no body that carried the Cappadocian congregations forward.
wanted: A dated source linking a present church to the Cappadocian congregations themselves.
openQuestion: Are the Cappadocian churches a period of the Greek Orthodox line, or a circle of fathers whose influence continues?

tradition: The imperial church from Constantine to Chalcedon
presentBody: the Catholic Church and the Orthodox churches of the Byzantine line
basis: An episode of a living tradition. The church of the emperors from 312 to 451 is the earlier life of the Catholic and Orthodox churches, which are alive today.

wanted: A dated source showing a community that continues the Bethlehem circle.
